2. The facts as stated in the petition, in short, are, that the late Haris Ahmed, husband of opposite party No.6, instituted Title Suit No. 34 of 1989 in the court of Upazila Assistant Judge praying for the declaration that he was entitled to get a deed of reconveyance from the petitioner on payment of Taka 5835.00 which was calculated after deducting two and a half years usufruct. The suit land comprises of an area of 0.24 decimals of land of plot No. 95 under Khatian No. 4 of Mouza Afzarkhil within Police Station Chatkhail. The owner, Haris Ahmed transferred the land to the defendant by a registered kabala on 15th Falgoon 1391 BS corresponding to 27.2.85 AD at a consideration of Taka 35.000.00 subject to a contemporaneous agreement for reconveyance. At the time of execution of the agreement the vendee promised to reconvey the land in favour of the vendor at any time within February 1988 on receipt of the kabala consideration. The plaintiff tendered the consideration money and demanded for reconveyance repeatedly but the defendant did not honour the agreement and on 2.8.87 finally declined to reconvey the land. Hence the suit for redemption of mortgage. The plaintiff sought relief under President's Order 88 of 1972 and President's Order 136 of 1972 and also President's Order 24 of 1972 and paid court fee of Taka 30.00 and the suit was valued at Taka 5835.00 on the ground that an mount of Taka 29,165.00 has been adjusted since 27.2.85 by way of enjoyment of usufruct of the land. 

 3. The defendants case is that the suit as framed and filed is not maintainable under the provision of President's Order 88/72 and 136/72 and 24/72 and also under sections 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and also that the suit is not properly valued. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Waliur Reja Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, cites the case of Nagendra Nath Sen Roy Vs. Saiyed Ali reported in 8 DLR 100 and contends that the above stated fundamental principle as to jurisdictional defect and its effect- on a court's authority to pass any decree should be read along with not only section 99 of Code of Civil Procedure but also with section 11 of the Suits Valuation Act. Section 11 which states that, notwithstanding anything in section 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an objection that a court which has no jurisdiction over a suit or an appeal has exercised it by reason of over valuation or under valuation, should not be entertained by an appellate Court except as provided in the section. It has been observed in the above mentioned case that" in view of the provision of section 11 of the Suits Valuation Act objection to a jurisdiction by a court based on over valuation should not be entertained by an appellate Court unless there was prejudice on merit".
